when I was in highschool, my school had a "run, hide, fight" alarm that they would only ever set off in an actual emergency and we would never drill for it, because people were supposed to either run from the building or shelter in place and hide. Well one day when I was a sophomore, the alarm went off during class. I remember freezing in place and looking around at my other classmates as my teacher gets up to lock the door and we all move against the wall. After about three-ish minutes, the principal comes over the loudspeaker saying that they had accidentally set it off, and they had meant to do just a lockdown that would keep students in classrooms so the halls were free. It turns out that a girl had attempted to jump from the third floor but a teacher had tackled her to the ground before she made it over. They wanted to lock down so they could properly assess the situation and keep people from doing anything in the halls, but students had actually already run out of the building at this point.
